_comment: Long-distance hiking trails of 40 miles or more that trail_emblems.json does NOT carry, found 2026-09-29 by four regional audits. 153 of them. This file is a CANDIDATE LIST, not a catalogue: nothing here has been loaded, registered or given an emblem, and the evidence grade on every row is the one the audit gave it rather than one this repository has re-earned.
_what_it_says_about_the_67: The emblem catalogue held 67 trails and read as a national list. It is not one. Against a 40-mile bar these four audits found 153 more with a named steward, and they did not finish - the northeast audit exhausted its search budget with Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, New Hampshire and Maine never swept, and no audit covered National Recreation Trails as a class. 67 was one pass, and reading it as a census was the mistake this file exists to correct.

_evidence_grades.measured: Re-run against a live GIS service during the audit. 23 rows. The strongest thing here.
_evidence_grades.steward: The maintaining organisation's own page gave the figure. 68 rows.
_evidence_grades.secondary: Only a non-steward source had it. 55 rows. Treat the mileage as approximate.
_evidence_grades.unverified: A specific doubt is named in the row's note. 7 rows. Do not publish these without checking.

_the_four_findings_that_matter_more_than.built_fraction_has_no_field_and_a_hiker_: AT LEAST 17 OF THESE 153 ARE NOT CONTINUOUSLY WALKABLE, and the schema has nowhere to say so. New Mexico's Rio Grande Trail is 500 miles planned and 88.5 designated. The Alaska Long Trail is 500 planned with a 1.3-mile segment under construction. Ala Kahakai is 175 miles of broken segments. A row showing a name and a mileage tells a hiker they can walk it end to end, and for these that is false. This is the FEATURES.md line about a confidently wrong prediction being more dangerous than an honest unknown, applied to a field that does not exist yet. Adding trails without adding this field would make the catalogue worse, not better.
_the_four_findings_that_matter_more_than.usfs_gis_miles_is_a_lower_bound_not_a_le: MEASURED during the audit: summing GIS_MILES over the USFS EDW TrailNFSPublish service gives 11.2 miles for the Wild Azalea Trail against a real 24-31, and 29.0 for the Uwharrie NRT against a claimed 40. It agreed with Land Between The Lakes' North/South Trail within 1.0 mile. The service's own description says data readiness varies between Forests and that Forests can provide no information. So a sum is how much tread has been MAPPED, not how long the trail is. If an exporter ever ingests this, that distinction has to survive into the export - a hiker shown '37.6 mi' for a 40-mile trail is being handed a data-coverage artefact in the voice of a measurement.
_the_four_findings_that_matter_more_than.overlap_is_tread_not_proximity: 17 rows share actual treadway with a trail already in the catalogue, and it is invisible from the name. The Great Eastern Trail CONTAINS the Pinhoti, the Cumberland Trail and Pine Mountain. The Lake Okeechobee Scenic Trail IS the Florida Trail's Okeechobee segment. The Collegiate Loop is the Colorado Trail plus the CDT. Kekekabic is now an official North Country Trail segment. Boundary Trail #533 overlaps the PNT; Rae Lakes overlaps the JMT; Timberline shares 11 miles with the PCT; the C&O Canal Towpath is the Potomac Heritage NST's designated route; Metacomet and Mattabesett are components of the New England Trail. lib/duplicates.py draws one path recorded twice once, and lib/concurrency.py draws two trails sharing treadway twice - which of those applies has to be decided per pair, and loading all 153 blind would double-count mileage and draw doubled lines.
_the_four_findings_that_matter_more_than.three_names_collide_outright: Adding these without qualifiers breaks GLOSSARY.md's disambiguation habit. JOHN MUIR TRAIL would mean three trails: the Sierra one already held, a 20.7-mile John Muir NRT in the Cherokee NF, and a 44-mile one in Big South Fork. MID STATE TRAIL (Pennsylvania, 327 mi, already held) against MIDSTATE TRAIL (Massachusetts, 92 mi). LINK TRAIL is a 40.3-mile trail in New York AND the former name of Pennsylvania's Standing Stone Trail, which is already held under its new name.

_the_highest_yield_next_step_is_not_more: Every audit reached the same conclusion independently: STATE GIS CLEARINGHOUSES return more verified trails per query than any amount of web search. Pennsylvania's DCNR service alone holds 91 named trails at 40 miles or more, and querying it produced seven Pennsylvania trails nobody would have thought to search for. The services below were each hit and confirmed live during the audit.

_what_the_audits_did_not_cover: Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, New Hampshire and Maine got no statewide sweep. National Recreation Trails as a class - reportedly 1300+ designated - were not enumerated by any audit. Neither were state trail systems in the states without a clearinghouse listed above. A fifth audit on the federal datasets was still running when this file was written.
_one_negative_result_worth_keeping: LOUISIANA HAS NO HIKING TRAIL THAT REACHES 40 MILES. Its longest footpath is the Wild Azalea Trail at 24-31 miles and its longest rail-trail is the Tammany Trace at 31. If per-state coverage is ever a target, Louisiana cannot meet a 40-mile bar and the gap is the state's, not the catalogue's.

_national_datasets._comment: What a fifth audit found when it stopped hunting trails one at a time and went looking for the datasets that enumerate them. Every count below came from a live request on 2026-09-29. THIS IS THE ANSWER TO 'as many trails as possible': the 153 candidates above are what searching found, and the services here are what would make searching unnecessary.

the_one_to_build_on.name: USGS The National Map - aggregated trails
the_one_to_build_on.why: The only national layer carrying a DESIGNATION field that enumerates the NSTs, NHTs and NRTs, alongside `name`, `lengthmiles`, `hikerpedestrian` and `primarytrailmaintainer`. GeoJSON export works directly - f=geojson with a where clause returns a valid FeatureCollection in WGS84, no conversion step.
the_one_to_build_on.licence: PUBLIC DOMAIN, stated by the service: 'The National Map download client allows free downloads of public domain transportation data'.
the_one_to_build_on.measured_designations: Grouping the 591,392-feature carto layer by `nationaltraildesignation` enumerates all 11 National Scenic Trails and 13 National Historic Trails in one query. NRT alone is 13,049 segments and 14,704 miles.
the_one_to_build_on.bulk: https://tnmaccess.nationalmap.gov/api/v1/products?datasets=National Transportation Dataset (NTD)&prodFormats=FileGDB - 57 per-state FileGDBs. Trails ship inside NTD; there is no trails-only product.

four_traps_in_it_all_measured.name_case_fragmentation_splits_one_trail: MEASURED: 'Appalachian National Scenic Trail' sums to 1,012.0 miles over 1,979 segments while 'APPALACHIAN TRAIL' sums separately to 440.3 over 250. The Continental Divide splits three ways - 869.1, 371.3 and 298.7 miles under three spellings. Normalise case and alias BEFORE grouping, or publish one trail as three, each at a fraction of its length. This is the exact failure mode `_the_four_findings` above describes for built fraction: a number in the voice of a measurement that is really an artefact.
four_traps_in_it_all_measured.networklength_is_not_the_trail: It is the length of the connected network a segment belongs to. Two A.T. segments returned 11,412.16 and 45.33 in the same query. Use SUM(lengthmiles). Never surface networklength as a distance.
four_traps_in_it_all_measured.string_sentinels_for_null: `nationaltraildesignation` holds literal 'Null' (2,472 rows) and '<Null>' (8,572) beside real nulls. `hikerpedestrian` holds BOTH 'Y' (138,741) and 'Yes' (139,662). A filter matching one spelling silently drops half the trails.
four_traps_in_it_all_measured.water_trails_are_mixed_in: The designated list at 50+ miles is topped by the Florida Circumnavigational Paddling Trail at 914.2 miles. Filter on hikerpedestrian or trailtype, not length. Generic names aggregate wrongly too - 'Social Trail' sums to 336.6 miles across 2,033 unrelated segments.

national_recreation_trails_the_roster_ex.measured: LengthMile is populated on EVERY row - zero nulls, which is rare. 70 trails at 100+ miles, 143 at 50+, 338 at 20+. TrailType splits Backcountry 853, Frontcountry 148, Urban 72, Rail Trail 72, and 85 water-trail rows to exclude.
national_recreation_trails_the_roster_ex.geometry_problem: The roster is POINTS. The companion line layer covers only 731 of the 1,358 (54%) and is four years staler. NRT centrelines have to be joined to TNM by name.
national_recreation_trails_the_roster_ex.THE_LICENCE_GAP: NONE STATED. Both items' licenseInfo and accessInformation are empty, and American Trails is a private nonprofit, so public domain is not the default. This is the single dataset most worth having and the only one here with no terms at all. ASK BEFORE SHIPPING - it is a one-email question of exactly the kind PCTA answered on its media page.

agency_services_with_their_traps.name: USFS EDW TrailNFSPublish
agency_services_with_their_traps.licence: A disclaimer, not a restriction - accconst is 'None'. US federal work.
agency_services_with_their_traps.trap: `national_trail_designation` does NOT mean NST or NHT. 80,917 of 86,417 features have it above zero, and sampled rows include 'BIG SPRINGS', 'SARDINE SNOWMOBILE' and '235 ROAD'. Filtering on it to find scenic trails returns nearly the whole layer.

agency_services_with_their_traps.name: NPS Public Trails
agency_services_with_their_traps.licence: No restriction stated; US federal work.
agency_services_with_their_traps.trap: NO LENGTH FIELD. Shape__Length comes back in DEGREES - an A.T. segment reads 0.348 - despite the response declaring WKID 102100. Never surface it as a distance. All 31,491 rows are already PUBLICDISPLAY-filtered, so no extra screening is needed.

agency_services_with_their_traps.name: BLM National GTLF Public Display
agency_services_with_their_traps.licence: No restriction stated; US federal work.
agency_services_with_their_traps.trap: The commonly-cited BLM_Natl_GTLF_Public URL 404s, and BLM_Natl_GTLF carries only 10,382 features - a recreation subset. This is the real one. BLM has the CLEANEST designation filter of any agency: ROUTE_SPCL_DSGNTN_TYPE literally spells 'National Scenic Trail'. Values are dirty though - 'N/A', 'NONE', 'NRT' and empty string appear alongside the full spellings.

agency_services_with_their_traps.name: NPS ANST_Centerline
agency_services_with_their_traps.licence: copyright 'National Park Service Appalachian National Scenic Trail & Appalachian Trail Conservancy, 2023'
agency_services_with_their_traps.trap: None found. Better sourced than the A.T. in TNM, and it is the layer this repository already reads.

_national_datasets.there_is_no_single_nst_service: CHECKED AND STATED CONCRETELY: mapservices.nps.gov/NationalDatasets holds exactly five datasets and none is a national trails-system layer. The NPS AGOL org's 1,457 services carry per-trail layers only. TNM's designation field IS the consolidation, and nothing else is.

openstreetmap.licence: ODbL - attribution AND share-alike on derived databases. The only dataset here with a share-alike obligation. Do not merge OSM geometry into a database shipped under other terms without advice.
openstreetmap.measured: 3,374 US relations at type=route + route=hiking; 428 network=nwn; 718 network=rwn. Only 92 national or international routes carry a `distance` tag, so OSM will not supply lengths for most.
openstreetmap.THE_TRAP_THAT_MATTERS: THE FLAGSHIP TRAILS ARE type=superroute, NOT type=route. Relation 1225378 fetched directly from the OSM API is the Pacific Crest Trail, tagged type=superroute with operator=Pacific Crest Trail Association. A query filtering ['type'='route'] - the form in most published recipes, and the form that produced the 3,374 figure - SILENTLY EXCLUDES IT. Query both.
openstreetmap.better_path: Waymarked Trails API, undocumented but working: hiking.waymarkedtrails.org/api/v1/list/search and /details/relation/{id}. Carries route.length in metres and a ready-made NAT/REG/LOC classification. The PCT reads 4,222,324 m = 2,624 mi against PCTA's ~2,650. Search has no country filter, so it resolves a known trail by name but cannot enumerate US trails.

_national_datasets.one_state_licence_blocker: IDAHO. Quoted from its item licenseInfo: 'Not for commercial use and may not be used in 3rd party apps without source attribution.' It names third-party apps specifically, so Idaho's 57,932-feature trails layer is the one state dataset here that cannot simply be ingested - and Idaho is where the 995-mile Idaho Centennial Trail is. New Jersey's NJDEP Data Distribution Agreement is a conditional grant too. Connecticut is CC0 and unambiguously safe.
_national_datasets.deduplication_order_suggested_by_the_aud: TNM as the spine, since it already aggregates USFS and most state contributions. Override with the NPS per-trail centrelines for the NSTs, which are better sourced. NRT roster for the 1,358 names and their lengths, licence permitting. BLM only for routes on BLM land TNM misses. OSM last and separately, because of ODbL.
_national_datasets.what_this_audit_could_not_reach: services.nationalmap.gov returned 502 through the egress proxy, twice - untested, not confirmed absent. The Partnership for the National Trails System's webmapping application is behind a bot wall. OSM iwn, lwn and route=foot counts are untested; the Overpass mirror degraded. The state survey covers 8 states with live counts plus 8 confirmed negatives, not 50.
